_doc: The standard switching plan (ACCOUNTS_PLAN_BUILD_STANDARD_SWITCHING), read by switching_plan.py and slot_allocator.py. Rules are data; each carries its provenance: [O] owner's words, [C] his question-card pick, [D] delegated (ours, under design/RimMandrake/delegation_policy.md), [A] agent proposal he has not ruled. Account names are the switcher's non-secret registry labels (~/.claude-accounts/accounts.tsv); reset times are NEVER written here: they are read from account_usage.py every pass.
_owner: [O] 2026-10-28 10:15 PDT: 'Use up both lukas.mandrake and mandrake.system of course down to ~2% for safety. Make sure not to overshoot and get stuck even if there is a surprise long-running subagent. then go idle until 1pm when you switch over to system.mandrake. Once steven.lewis resets, switch over to it and use it until 50%. Then use up system.mandrake to 2%, then lukas.mandrake to 2%. That's our first "standard switching plan."'
_order: [O] 2026-10-28 10:15 (see _owner): 'Once steven.lewis resets, switch over to it and use it until 50%. Then use up system.mandrake to 2%, then lukas.mandrake to 2%.' A fixed priority: the engine burns the FIRST account in this list that is eligible (measured, fresh, inside its window, above its line). steven is eligible only inside his window after his reset, down to leave_pct_left. When system resets, the machine goes to system even if lukas still has budget; a lower account's budget that expires first is given up (the owner 2026-10-28, on being left on lukas at 13:00: 'awkward').

steven._leave_pct_left: [C] 2026-10-28 10:20 card, Steven: 'Leave at 52% left' (his 10:15 words: 'use it until 50%'; the 2 points are the overshoot margin).
steven._window_h_after_reset: [O] 2026-10-27 'Dispatcher can use Steve up to 50% after a fresh reset only'; the 48 h reading of 'fresh' is [A] (slot_rules.json lent_accounts.steven.prefer_start_of_week_h). Outside this window the engine never switches to steven and switches off him if live.

floors._doc: [C] 2026-10-28 15:33 card, Drain floor: 'Drain to 0% (Recommended)' (settles the 10:15 'down to ~2%' vs the relayed 11:2x 'let it hit 0%'). [O] relayed by the coordinator 2026-10-28 11:2x: 'If it's actually safe to switch (is that because it goes through tailscale or something?) even when we hit 0%, then let it hit 0%. I thought it would lock us out'. The switch is local (claude-account swaps the credential file; no model tokens, no Tailscale), so an account we switch away from burns to 0%. [D] delegated: ops threshold (card 10:20, Floor: '[No preference]'; restated by the coordinator 11:2x): the account we idle on until a reset keeps 2%, so the owner can still talk to a seat while we wait. blind_zero_pct [R] coordinator 11:2x: once an account's last MEASURED reading is at or under 1%, a blind reading (failed /usage, usage-limit error, ESTIMATE, stale) counts as 0% and triggers the switch: never sit waiting on a meter that cannot read an exhausted account.

_soft_margin_pct: [C] card 10:20, Overshoot: 'Soft line, then hard stop'. At line + 2%: the allocator gives every seat 0 new helpers and the notice tells running ones to publish and finish.
_switch_lead_min: [A] a switch that a reset will cause (system at its reset, steven at his) raises the same soft notice this many minutes before the reset, so work is published before the windows close.

fresh._doc: [A] (brief 2026-10-28): within near_pct of a line, the engine polls the meter itself rather than trust a reading older than max_age_min.

_window_margin_min: [R] GPT review round 9: a windowed account (steven) is no switch target in the last 10 min of its window, so a slow arm + use never lands after the window closed (live there, it is switched away early).
_pool_pacing: [C] card 10:20, Pacing: 'Pace the whole pool BECAUSE it spreads out the human review time cleanly to inform the process in a timely manner.' slot_allocator paces on what this plan will still spend (steven down to its leave line inside its window, the others to their floors) over the hours to each deadline.

exceptions._why: [O] owner, by question card 2026-11-17 ~10:40 PST (system 13% left, steven 55%, lukas 2%; the standing plan would idle at system's floor until system's Wed reset): 'Current rule until the reset: Use this account, then switch to Steve, but keep the one mod at a time policy so we use it slowly. We need to leave space for Steven too.' So system burns first (order), then steven outside his window. [D] delegated (Conductor, CONDUCTOR_AUTHORITY_DECIDE_NO_ASKING_MOM): he gave no number for 'leave space for Steven', so steven stops at 35% left; the exception ends at steven's next reset (read from the meter, ends_at_reset_of) or at `until` (Wed 2026-11-18 14:00 PST, his reset as metered on the day), whichever is first. [O] 2026-11-17 ~5:22 PM PST: 'please move to Steven when we get to 1% not 0%', so system's line is 1% left for this exception. After it the standing plan applies unchanged. Ledger: RIMMANDRAKE_EXPLORE_OPERATIONS_OPTIONS_AFTER_WEDNESDAY_RESET. The one-run-at-a-time limit is maturation_dispatch.json max_live 1 (84472234cb26), not this file.

_exceptions: [D] dated, self-expiring exceptions to the rules above (switching_plan.at(): the plan in force at a time). Each needs an id, `from` and `until` as ISO times with their UTC offset (at most 7 days apart), a `_why` with its provenance, and changes `order` (a reordering of the standing accounts) and/or `accounts.<name>.leave_pct_left` / `window_h_after_reset`; optional `ends_at_reset_of` ends it at that account's first reset after `from`, read from the meter. The guard (exception_problems) refuses a broken one, and overlapping ones, which are then never applied: the standing plan stands and every decision names the refusal (exception_refused). slot_allocator.lent_allowance reads the same exception for a lent account. An expired exception is inert and may be deleted.
